result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers clearly recommend B and explain that a proportional font and collapsed whitespace break stack-trace indentation and timing columns, so they score about the same on most items. Answer B states the core point more directly: the blog is prose and the log is machine output, so they should look different. Its suggested tweaks (tab-size and a constrained pane width so overflow-x actually scrolls) are also slightly more practical. Answer A's tweaks (tab-size and turning off ligatures) are also modest and sound, but it ties the prose-versus-log distinction less clearly to the content. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend B clearly and give sound, content-specific reasons why A and C break alignment and indentation, so they are very close. Answer B edges ahead: it handles the teammate's branding concern by moving brand consistency to the header, colors and chrome, and it points to existing CI log viewers as the convention developers expect. Its tweaks are concrete and modest (tab-size and disabling ligatures) and come as ready-to-use CSS.
